slides.title: Big-O Notation
slides.content:
# Time Complexity ⏱️

How does runtime grow with input size?

## Common Complexities

| Big-O | Name | Example |
|-------|------|---------|
| O(1) | Constant | Array access |
| O(log n) | Logarithmic | Binary search |
| O(n) | Linear | Loop through array |
| O(n log n) | Linearithmic | Merge sort |
| O(n²) | Quadratic | Nested loops |
| O(2ⁿ) | Exponential | Recursive fib |

## Examples

```python
# O(1) - Constant
def get_first(arr):
    return arr[0]

# O(n) - Linear
def find_max(arr):
    max_val = arr[0]
    for x in arr:
        if x > max_val:
            max_val = x
    return max_val

# O(n²) - Quadratic
def pairs(arr):
    for i in arr:
        for j in arr:
            print(i, j)
```

slides.title: Space Complexity
slides.content:
# Space Complexity 💾

How much memory does the algorithm use?

## Examples

```python
# O(1) Space - In-place
def swap(arr, i, j):
    arr[i], arr[j] = arr[j], arr[i]

# O(n) Space - New array
def double(arr):
    result = [x * 2 for x in arr]
    return result

# O(n) Space - Recursion stack
def factorial(n):
    if n <= 1:
        return 1
    return n * factorial(n - 1)
```

## Trade-offs

| Approach | Time | Space |
|----------|------|-------|
| Brute force | Slow | Low |
| Memoization | Fast | High |
| Optimal | Fast | Low |

> 💡 **Often we trade space for time!**
